standard_prerequisites.name: Pullback of a divisor of a rational function along a flat morphism, and infinite sums of rational equivalences
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, labels lemma-prepare-flat-pullback-rational-equivalence (proof line 3208) and remark-infinite-sums-rational-equivalences (proof line 3213)

core_obligations: Unwind rational equivalence into a locally finite family of principal divisors on integral closed subschemes and observe that the pulled back family is locally finite (proof lines 3181-3195).

Form the fibre products over the source, rewrite the pulled back sum as a sum of pushforwards of pulled back divisors, and use the prepared flat pullback statement to see that each term is rationally trivial (proof lines 3197-3210).
Conclude for the sum by the statement on infinite sums of rational equivalences (proof lines 3211-3213).
proof_roadmap: Unwind and check local finiteness (proof lines 3181-3195).
Rewrite over the fibre products and use the prepared pullback statement (proof lines 3197-3210).
Upgrade to the locally finite sum (proof lines 3211-3213).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the functoriality of rational equivalence under flat pullback: rationally equivalent cycles pull back to rationally equivalent cycles, with the relative dimension shift (statement lines 3172-3179, tag 02S1). The proof unwinds rational equivalence into a locally finite family of principal divisors, verifies that the pulled back family is locally finite, passes to the fibre products over the source and rewrites the pulled back sum as a sum of pushforwards of pulled back principal divisors, each of which is rationally trivial by the prepared flat pullback statement, and then concludes for the sum. The rewriting through the fibre products is the substance, so the claim is H2.
